main_text.p: pœnitet me hujus, μεταμέλομαι ὅτι τύ- πτω, pœnitentia hujus ducor: δεῖ μοι χρημάτων, opus est mihi pecuniis, δέο- μαι χρημάτων, opus habeo pecuniis.
main_text.head: Cap. 21. De infinito substantivo.
main_text.p: Verbum substantivum regit ante & post eundem casum: modo nominativum: Xenoph. νομίζω, ἐὰν ἵππος γίνωμαι, ἀν' Αἴγυπτος πλοῦς ἔσταθαι [?], exisi- mo, si equus fiam, homo volucris fore: id est, credo me fore hominem volucrem. Demoft. ὅταν φῇ δημοτικὸς εἶ[?], quando dixerit popularis esse. Idem, Μαύσωλος φίλος εἶ[?] φάσκων Ῥοδίων, Mausolus dicens esse amicus Rhodiorum. Sic Ovid.
Modó genitivum. Plat. ἡ δόμυλλ' αὐτῆς δὲ τὴν ποίησιν οἰομένων ἢ πάλλα σοφωτάτων εἶ[?]

page.notes: Greek passages are printed with accents and breathings that are hard to read at this scan resolution; the marked words (εἶ, ἔσταθαι, the last Plato line) are doubtful. The Ovid verse "Esse Jovis pronepos" is printed indented as a quotation. No text in the margins.
